Chloe Slater has turned online scrutiny into a single with 'I've Never Felt So Hated'

Debut album 'Riot Youth' arrives 9th October, with a UK and European tour to follow.

The Lowdown

(everything wotcha need to know)

  1. +Chloe Slater's shared new single 'I've Never Felt So Hated', written about the online scrutiny and mental health struggles she's faced.
  2. +The track explores how short-form media encourages snap judgments: "Everything has to be polarised and divisive to get clicks, and the result is such black and white thinking."
  3. +It's the latest from her debut album 'Riot Youth', out 9th October via Stolen Juice (AWAL), following singles 'UGLY', 'Southern Youth' and 'Mother Nature's Killing Spree'.
  4. +Chloe tours the UK and Europe in November and December, including London's Scala on 10th November, with £1 from every ticket going to Music Declares Emergency's Plus 1 initiative.

Chloe Slater has shared new single ‘I’ve Never Felt So Hated’, the latest track from her debut album ‘Riot Youth’, out 9th October via Stolen Juice (AWAL).

The song was written in response to the scrutiny Chloe has faced online, and the way short-form media can encourage strangers to form definitive opinions about people from very little information. “This song is centred around my mental health struggles as a result of internet scrutiny,” she explains. “It's about how easy it is in 2026 to watch a twenty-second video, or read a comment and form an opinion on someone with a complete lack of context.”

“In the digital age of short-form media, it is so difficult to form nuanced opinions,” she continues. “Everything has to be polarised and divisive to get clicks, and the result is such black and white thinking: it's true love or extreme hate.” The track arrives alongside a video directed by Bonnie MacRae.

‘I've Never Felt So Hated’ follows recent singles ‘UGLY’, ‘Southern Youth’ and ‘Mother Nature’s Killing Spree’. Chloe will take ‘Riot Youth’ on a UK and European headline tour this November and December, including a London date at Scala on 10th November, with £1 from every ticket donated to Music Declares Emergency’s Plus 1 initiative.
